comment: Pinned llama.cpp runtime payload shipped under resources/llama by scripts/vendor-llama.mjs. The binaries are build output and are NOT committed; this manifest and its SHA-256 pin are. Only the Windows x64 CPU build is pinned for now: the local-model feature looks for llama-server.exe there and reports the runtime as missing on platforms this manifest does not cover. Add a release by adding an entry here, then run the script.

releases.note: The archive extracts flat (no top-level directory). llama-server.exe is a thin launcher: the server itself is in llama-server-impl.dll, which loads llama.dll, llama-common.dll, mtmd.dll, ggml.dll, ggml-base.dll, libomp.dll and one ggml-cpu-<isa>.dll selected at runtime, so every *.dll stays. The archive ships one ggml-cpu-*.dll per x86-64 ISA level (the best match is picked at startup), which is why the CPU payload is larger than a single-library build. The other llama-*.exe tools and every llama-*-impl.dll they load are dropped to keep the installer small. LICENSE-LLVM-OpenMP is kept because libomp.dll is LLVM OpenMP; the llama.cpp trees themselves are MIT, as recorded above.
